To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present a novel subspace appearance model that is able to model the appearance of non-rigid deformable objects that can undergo occlusion, and that we demonstrate the usefulness of this model in two applications, structured inpainting and object transfer.
we introduce a subspace appearance model that can handle non-rigid objects with complex, non-linear occlusion and that it can be used for structured inpainting and transfer of appearance.
we propose a new subspace model which can be conditioned on context to capture the appearance of deformable objects with complex occlusions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning appearance models for objects that are not necessarily rigid and whose appearance may change significantly due to occlusions.
the problem of modeling object appearance using Context Conditioned Component Analysis (CCCA).
the development of subspace models for the appearance of non-rigid, occluded objects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our model can learn a subspace of the object appearance and then use that subspace to generate a new appearance of the object.

our model allows for the appearance of non-rigid objects to be captured and manipulated in a manner that is similar in many ways to the appearance of rigid objects, but which allows for the more complex appearance of non-rigidity and occlusions to be captured and transferred in a natural and intuitive manner.
our method can be used to model the appearance of complex objects that cannot be modeled by existing subspace models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are extending the applicability of subspace appearance modeling to non-rigid, occluded objects by conditioning the appearance models on a shape-dependent context.
our model can be used to model the appearance of objects that have complex, non-linear structures.
the proposed model is able to model the appearance of a set of visual objects with complex occlusions, deformable parts and different numbers of parts, without requiring any alignment of the objects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the context-conditioned model can be used to model the appearance of objects that are not well suited to subspace models.
by conditioning the appearance model on a shape dependent, context variable, we can model the appearance of complex objects without requiring image-space alignment.
we can model the appearance of complex, non-rigid, occluded objects using a subspace model, which is a significant advance over existing methods.
